safety.title: Safety
safety.sub: What ChatGPT may touch on this PC, and what it must ask about first.
safety.confirmSub: A pop-up asks you before the actions below run. No answer in time means Deny.
safety.lastFolder: Keep at least one folder ChatGPT can work in.
safety.always: Always blocked: Bridgerator's own settings, key, snapshots and program files — so nothing here can be switched off behind your back.
safety.onlyThese: ChatGPT can work only in these folders
safety.read_onlyHint: Read only: ChatGPT can look and search; nothing can be changed, the terminal is off.
safety.filesHint: Files: ChatGPT can read and change files; the terminal is off.
safety.fullHint: Full: files and the terminal (default). Use the switches below to limit it.
safety.sensitiveHint: Startup programs, PowerShell profiles, .ssh, cloud logins, AppData. Off by default.
safety.recycleHint: When ChatGPT deletes with a simple command (del, rd, Remove-Item, rm), the files go to the Recycle Bin. On by default.
safety.recycleNoBin: No Recycle Bin on that drive
safety.recycleNoBinHint: Network drives and many USB sticks have none: Bridgerator asks you on this PC before deleting for good.
safety.recycleNet: A safety net, not a guarantee: scripts, pipelines and other programs that delete are not caught.
safety.snapshotsHint: A copy of each file before ChatGPT changes, moves or deletes it. Kept only on this PC. On by default.
safety.bigFileHint: A bigger file is changed without a copy (marked "no undo").
safety.clearSnapsText: Changes made so far can no longer be undone. Files themselves are not touched.
safety.fuse: Pause on mass deletes or moves
safety.fuseHint: If ChatGPT deletes or moves many files within a minute, Bridgerator pauses and asks you whether to continue. Off by default.
safety.scheduled_scriptsHint: Before ChatGPT puts a script on a schedule or changes one

settings.keepAwake: Keep this PC awake while ChatGPT works

settings.keepAwakeHint: While ChatGPT works or the task queue has tasks, on mains power only. The screen can still turn off. On by default.

start.label: Getting started
start.title: Getting started
start.intro: Bridgerator lets ChatGPT work with files and programs on this PC, inside the folders you allow.
steps: Keep this PC on and Bridgerator running (green icon in the tray).
In ChatGPT, open Bridgerator from the apps menu.
Say “Set up Bridgerator”. ChatGPT asks a few questions and you confirm the settings here.

queue.label: Task queue
queue.title: Using the task queue
queue.intro: The queue is a checklist for ChatGPT. It takes the first task, does it, marks it done or failed with a short note, then moves to the next one.
steps: Add tasks here, or ask ChatGPT to plan the work and add the steps itself.
Attach files or folders to a task so ChatGPT knows where to look.
In ChatGPT, say “Work through my Bridgerator queue”. Watch the ticks appear here.
Edit, reorder or delete tasks any time. A failed task shows why it failed.

ChatGPT may ask you to allow an action in the chat; the task waits for your answer. If a task stalls, Bridgerator shows a notice. "Selected model is at capacity" is ChatGPT's own error: press Retry in the chat or pick another model; the queue keeps its place.

agents.label: AI ↔ AI
agents.title: Hand tasks between AIs
agents.intro: ChatGPT can hand a task to an AI agent installed on this PC — Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI — and another AI can hand tasks to ChatGPT through the queue.
steps: ChatGPT → agent: install the agent and sign in once in a terminal. Bridgerator finds it on the Agents page (on by default).
Say in ChatGPT what to do and in which folder. The agent works there with your own subscription and ChatGPT gets its answer and the list of changed files.
Undo a whole delegated task on the Agents page. Limits (what an agent may do, time, tasks at once) are there too.
Another AI → ChatGPT: connect it to Bridgerator, ask it to add tasks to the queue for ChatGPT with a result file, then say “Work through my Bridgerator queue” in ChatGPT.
agents.tip: Ask Claude Code to review D:\Projects\site and tell me what it found

confirm.label: Confirmations
confirm.title: Confirm on this PC
confirm.intro: When it is on, a pop-up asks you before ChatGPT deletes files or runs risky system commands. It is off by default.
steps: Turn it on in Safety and choose what needs your OK.
Allow runs it once; Allow 10 min stops asking for ten minutes.
Allow always turns that check off. Turn it back on in Safety.
No answer in two minutes means Deny. Nothing runs.

folders.label: Folders
folders.title: Folders ChatGPT can use
folders.intro: By default ChatGPT may work in all folders. Limit it to specific folders in Safety. Read-only folders can be opened and searched, never changed.
steps: To limit ChatGPT, add the folders you work in, for example Documents or D:\Work.
Mark folders with photos or archives as read-only.
Turn on "Protect sensitive folders" to block startup programs, PowerShell profiles, saved keys and AppData. Bridgerator's own files are always blocked.

undo.label: Undo & Recycle Bin
undo.title: Undo ChatGPT's changes
undo.intro: Before ChatGPT changes, moves or deletes a file, Bridgerator keeps a copy on this PC for 7 days. Simple delete commands send files to the Recycle Bin.
steps: Open Recent and click Undo next to an action, or "Undo AI changes…" for a whole task or batch.
A file someone changed after ChatGPT is left as it is and listed.
Limits and switches are in Safety → Undo & Recycle Bin.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.title: What leaves this PC
privacy.intro: Your files and command output travel to ChatGPT through our server over an encrypted connection (TLS). The server does not store them.
steps: Recent actions and the task queue are stored only on this PC.
Anonymous stats (version, tool counts) can be turned off in Settings.
Your account shows only the tool name, time and result of each call.

trouble.label: Troubleshooting
trouble.title: Something is not working
trouble.intro: Most problems are fixed by running the install command again. It keeps your settings.
steps: Grey tray icon: check the internet connection, then choose Resume.
ChatGPT says the PC is offline: make sure this PC is awake and Bridgerator is running.
Still stuck: send the log (%APPDATA%\Bridgerator\bridge.log) to support.

setup.title: ChatGPT suggests Bridgerator settings
setup.text: Nothing changes until you click Apply.

talk.label: Talk to ChatGPT
talk.title: Talk to ChatGPT
talk.intro: Say these in any ChatGPT chat that has Bridgerator connected. Several chats can work at the same time.
talk.setupHint: ChatGPT asks a few questions and suggests settings; you confirm them on this PC.
talk.add: Add these tasks to my Bridgerator queue: …
talk.addHint: List the tasks after the colon, one per line.
talk.workHint: ChatGPT takes the tasks one by one and marks each done or failed.
talk.continueHint: In a new chat: picks up where another chat stopped.
talk.showHint: Folders, confirmations, notifications — what is set now.
talk.confirmOnHint: Raising protection applies at once; turning it off needs your OK on this PC.
talk.delegate: Ask Claude Code to review this folder and report back: D:\Projects\site
talk.delegateHint: ChatGPT hands the task to an AI agent installed on this PC (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) and brings back its answer. See Agents.

auto.title: Automations
auto.sub: Scripts that Windows runs on a schedule — also when no chat is open, without using calls. Scripts and results stay on this PC.

auto.autoClean: Every Monday move downloads older than 30 days to the Recycle Bin
auto.autoReport: Make a disk space report every Friday
auto.notify: Notify me when ChatGPT schedules a script

batch.text: Allowed actions run without a separate question for 30 minutes. The others still ask.

agents.modeHint: Full = the agent's own widest permissions, inside the chosen folder. In a read-only folder an agent only reads.
